name: Szechenyi Thermal Bath
who: Neo-Baroque thermal bath complex with 15+ indoor and outdoor pools, open daily on a walk-in day-ticket model.
why: Budapest's largest and most photographed bath, the default bucket-list soak in the city.

name: Rudas Baths
who: 16th-century Ottoman-era bathhouse with a domed octagonal pool, day tickets plus weekend night bathing.
why: The best-preserved Turkish bath in Budapest, with the tradition's defining domed-pool architecture.

name: Lukacs Baths
who: Medicinal thermal bath and pool complex favored by locals, open daily with standard day access.
why: The regulars' alternative to Szechenyi, now more prominent while Gellert and Kiraly sit closed.

name: Veli Bej Bath
who: 16th-century Ottoman bathhouse restored and reopened in 2012, small domed pool plus four side pools, daily day tickets.
why: A quiet, authentic Ottoman-era bath that has gained weight now that Gellert and Kiraly are shut for renovation.

name: Friedrichsbad
who: 1877 Roman-Irish bathing house running a fixed 17-step nude circuit, day and session tickets.
why: The definitive European Roman-Irish bath ritual, still run in an unchanged Belle Epoque hall.
reach: IG 18K (verified 2026-08, shared account with Caracalla Spa)

name: Caracalla Spa
who: 1985-built swimwear-required thermal pool and sauna complex next to Friedrichsbad, day access.
why: The contemporary counterpart that carries Baden-Baden's thermal tradition to a broader, mixed-swimwear public.

name: Cagaloglu Hamami
who: 1741 Ottoman hamam near Hagia Sophia with a grand marble hararet chamber, walk-in sessions and treatments.
why: Nearly 300 years of continuous hamam service in one of Istanbul's grandest bath halls.

name: Kilic Ali Pasa Hamami
who: 1580 Mimar Sinan-designed hamam in Tophane, restored single-dome hararet, walk-in sessions and treatments.
why: A Sinan-designed bathhouse restored to its original grandeur, an architecture-first hamam experience.

name: Cemberlitas Hamami
who: 1584 Sinan-designed hamam next to the Grand Bazaar, twin men's/women's sections, walk-in sessions.
why: Often called the best-known Turkish bath in Istanbul, a Sinan landmark still bathing tourists and locals daily.

name: Hurrem Sultan Hamami
who: 1556 twin hamam commissioned by Hurrem Sultan between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque, guided day sessions.
why: A sultan-commissioned double hamam standing on Istanbul's single most historic square.

name: Sanduny Banya
who: 1808 Russian banya palace with Baroque-decorated halls, several ticket classes for day/session bathing.
why: Russia's most famous banya and the historic reference point for the entire banya tradition.

name: Banya No.1
who: Russian-style banya and spa club opened 2016 (Hoxton flagship), public sessions plus membership.
why: Brought authentic banya ritual culture to a Western capital and has since expanded to Paris and Tbilisi.

name: Thermae Bath Spa
who: 2006-built spa on the UK's only natural hot springs, open-air rooftop pool, day sessions and treatments.
why: The sole legal way to bathe in the naturally hot water that made the city of Bath a Roman and Georgian spa town.

name: QC Terme Bagni Vecchi di Bormio
who: Roman/medieval-origin Alpine thermal complex with historic bathing caves plus QC Terme's spa circuit, day tickets.
why: Thermal bathing on a site used since Roman times, now QC Terme's flagship historic property.

name: Terme di Saturnia
who: Sulfur hot-spring resort on an Etruscan/Roman thermal site, five-star spa with day-access tickets.
why: A thermal source used for millennia, now anchoring one of Italy's best-known spa resorts.

name: Hammam Al Andalus
who: Moorish-revival hammam built 2004 in Granada's Albaicin, hot/cold bath circuit plus treatments, day sessions.
why: Recreated Andalusian hammam architecture that revived Spain's Moorish bathing culture for modern visitors.

name: Royal Mansour Hammam
who: Palace-hotel hammam in marble treatment suites; non-guests can book the hammam and treatments by advance reservation.
why: The most architecturally lavish hammam in Marrakech, set inside a five-star riad-palace.
warning: Hammam and spa treatments are bookable by non-guests; pool and garden access stays reserved for hotel guests.

name: La Mamounia Spa
who: Legendary hotel spa with twin hammams; non-guests book a Pass Detente day package (treatment/hammam plus lunch).
why: Marrakech's most iconic hotel spa, pairing 1920s glamour with a traditional hammam ritual.
warning: General day pass is gone; non-guest access now requires booking a treatment, hammam, or the paid Pass Detente package.

name: Amalienbad
who: 1926 Art Deco/Art Nouveau public bathhouse and pool with sauna and wellness area, daily day tickets.
why: The grandest surviving bathhouse of 'Red Vienna,' a working monument to 1920s municipal bathing culture.

name: Orbeliani Baths (Chreli-Abano)
who: Historic domed sulfur bathhouse in Abanotubani, renovated and reopened 2017, private rooms plus communal hall, day bookings.
why: The most photogenic of Tbilisi's brick-domed sulfur bathhouses, still fed by the city's natural hot springs.
